question.leadin: This group mocked the US, France, and UK forces during a mock funeral in Khost.
question.text: Name this group that took over a certain country after defeating a resistance movement in Panjshir Province. This group, which takes its name from the word "students," is largely led by Pashtun militants.
question.clue: It was opposed by a contingent of non-Pashtun warlords known as the Northern Alliance.

swap.text: Kazakhstan has the longest coastline on this body of water which, despite its name, is the largest lake in the world. This lake also borders Russia, Azerbaijan, Iran, and Turkmenistan, and caviar is often procured from fish in this lake.
swap.answerHtml: Caspian Sea [or Kaspii Tenizi, or Hazar Denzi, or Hezer Denizi]
swap.clue: The world's first oil tanker sailed across this body of water from a port that produced half of the world's oil in 1900.

question.leadin: Following this man's brutal sack of Baghdad, he had human skulls stacked into giant pyramids.
question.text: Name this famously handicapped Central Asian conqueror of Mongol origin who conquered a massive empire before suddenly dying en route to an invasion of China.
question.clue: This man's victories at the Battles of the Kondurcha and Terek Rivers led to his defeat of Tokhtamysh and the Golden Horde.

swap.leadin: Give the following about the 1449 Tumu [tuh-MU] Crisis.
swap.text: The crisis involved a raid of 20,000 of these people, led by Esen Taishi, into Ming territory where they destroyed an unprepared army of half a million Ming soldiers. These people ruled the Yuan Dynasty, which was defeated by the Ming.
swap.clue: A kurultai was a military, political, and religious council used by this ethnic group to select their new rulers.

question.leadin: Answer the following about a powerful eastern empire's leaders.
question.text: This northwestern khanate was notably ruled by Batu Khan, and its "Blue" and "White" divisions were reunited by Tokhtamysh.
question.clue: The Zadonshchina ("zuh-DOAN-shih-nuh") recounts a defeat of this polity, earlier centralized by a unification of "Blue" and "White" branches by Tokhtamysh.

swap.leadin: The Yassa was an oral law code used by this empire.
swap.text: Name this empire founded by Genghis Khan whose successor states included the Yuan (YOO-un) dynasty.
swap.clue: This empire, which lost to the Mamluks at Ain Jalut, notoriously flung the bodies of plague-infested corpses with their counterweight trebuchets, spreading the Black Death.

question.text: This Central Asian proxy conflict between the British and Russian empires provided the justification for the war, as the British feared Dost Mohammad Khan would side with the Russians in a potential invasion of India.
question.clue: The Fortress of Orenburg was constructed in order to control the Kazakhs as part of this period, which also saw extended maneuvering over the rights to Sinkiang.

swap.leadin: This empire was formed in the 7th century AD following the end of the Zhangzhung kingdom.
swap.text: Name this ancient Himalayan empire which flourished until the 9th century and had a capital at Lhasa.
swap.clue: Ralpacan was one of this empire's Three Dharma Kings.

question.text: This republic on the Yenisey near Mongolia was independent, with its capital at Kyzyl, from 1921 to 1944.
question.clue: Under Chinese rule from 1757 to 1911, Russia helped it achieve independence in 1911 and annexed it in 1944.

swap.leadin: In the 1990s, this country's leader renamed the town of Janga for himself, Kerki for his father, and Yylanly ("yuh-lahn-luh") for his mother.
swap.text: Name this country where doctors were required to follow an oath to its president, Saparmurat Niyazov, instead of the Hippocratic Oath.
swap.clue: The Rukhnama, or "Book of Soul," was a propaganda work written by a former head of this state, Saparmurat Niyazov.

question.leadin: Zhang Qian's travels helped open up this trade route.
question.text: What pathway begun in the second century BCE eventually linked China to the Mediterranean?
question.clue: A 2015 best-selling history book by Peter Frankopan is titled for the plural form of this entity.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the tribe known as the Alans, who migrated to Europe in the late 4th and early 5th centuries.
swap.text: In the late 9th century, the Alans established an independent kingdom in this mountain range. A nation in this range is often recognized as the first to establish Christianity as its official religion, doing so in 301 A.D.
swap.clue: Bagrationi Dynasty rulers such as Tamar the Great led a kingdom based in this range.The Circassians were based in this range, near the site of a genocide that remains ignored underArticle 301 today.

question.text: The Ballad of Mulan instead depicts her fighting the Rouran ("roh-rahn"), who are the first historical people of note to use this title for their rulers. This Turkic title was also given to the leader of the Mongols.
question.clue: One of these figures destroyed the Khwarezmian cities of Urgench and Samarkand and established his capital at Karakorum.

swap.text: This group of Mongols captured the Zhengtong emperor of Ming during the Tumu Crisis. This tribe's historical confederation was composed of four tribes.
swap.clue: The Khoshut were one of four tribes comprising this Mongol subgroup, who rivaled the Tumeds and later founded the Kalmyk Khanate. A leader of these people captured the Zhengtong ("JUNG-tong") emperor in one military campaign.

question.leadin: One ruler of this city sentenced two British diplomats to its prison's infamous "bug pit" after they tried to ride into his palace on horseback and arrived without a gift for him.
question.text: Name this city, the capital of an emirate that lost control of nearby Samarkand when it was attacked by Russia along with the neighboring Khiva and Kokand khanates.
question.clue: A group modelled off the Young Turks invited the Soviet conquest of this city and was given prominent leadership positions in the short-lived Soviet republic centered on this city.

swap.text: Once the Red Army toppled Ungern von Sternberg, this early Mongolian leader liquidated Mongolian Buddhist institutions and clergy after pushing out Peljidiin Genden, who had denied Stalin's requests to do so.
swap.clue: With Shtern and Zukhov, this man commanded the winning side at the Battle of Khalkin Gol.

question.text: The author of History of the Hind, al-Biruni, traveled to India with the invading forces of Mahmud-i Zabuli, the first Sultan of this Turkic empire which broke off from the Samanids.
question.answerHtml: the Ghaznavid Empire [or Ghaznaviyan; Mahmud’s father Sabuktigin founded the dynasty but Mahmud was the first to call it a Sultanate]
question.clue: This empire whose first leader, Sabuktigin, was a slave before being promoted by Alptigin.

swap.leadin: The western movement of the Xiongnu confederacy pushed these people south, which in turn pushed the Sacae into the Greco-Bactrian Kingdom.
swap.text: Name these Tocharian-speaking nomads who, along with the Wusun, were visited by the Han diplomat Zhang Qian, who reported on their one hundred thousand horse archers.
swap.answerHtml: Yuezhi [accept Greater Yuezhi or Lesser Yuezhi; prompt on, but DO NOT REVEAL, Kushans]
swap.clue: This Central Asian people whose "Greater" branch migrated into the Ili Valley in the 160s BCE after the Xiongnu ("sh'yung-noo") defeated them. Kujula Kadphises ("koo-JOO-la kad-FYE-seez") later united these people and founded the Kushan Empire.

question.text: This Khereid princess became Genghis Khan's daughter-in-law when she married his youngest son Tolui. She was the mother of the khans Mongke, Kublai, and Hulagu.

swap.leadin: A member of this family abolished the longstanding beylik system in a series of westernizing reforms encouraged by his backer Catherine the Great.
swap.text: Name this family whose founder supposedly devised a three-pronged symbol known as the Tarak Tamga. That man's son defeated the last Khan of the Golden Horde and occupied Sarai.
swap.answerHtml: Giray [accept Hacı I Giray or Melek Haji Giray or Şahin Giray]
